summary.text: Paleomagnetism is the study of Earth's ancient magnetic fields as recorded in rocks, sediment and archaeological materials.
Certain magnetic minerals lock in the field's direction and strength when they form, revealing how the field behaved and where tectonic plates once sat.
Its evidence revived the idea of continental drift and helped turn it into the modern theory of plate tectonics.

facts.label: Key mineral
facts.value: Magnetite, which can record past polarity

facts.label: Archaeological records
facts.value: Pottery kilns, hearths and burned adobe buildings

items.prompt: Basalt lava erupts, crystallizes, and keeps cooling. At what point does its magnetite record the direction of Earth's field?

options.label: The instant the lava leaves the volcano
Only once sediment buries it
As it cools through its Curie temperature
Whenever lightning hits it later

items.explain: Iron-titanium oxides in basalt can preserve the field's direction as the rock cools through their Curie temperature, about 580 °C for magnetite.

items.prompt: An archaeologist uncovers an ancient fireplace with no written records nearby. Why could its baked clay help date it?

options.label: Heat made the clay keep a record of the field
Heat stops clay from ever changing again
Fire leaves soot that builds up each year
Baked clay holds onto rings like a tree

items.explain: Hearths and kilns can hold a thermoremanent magnetization, and studying it in archaeological materials is called archaeomagnetic dating.

items.prompt: Polar wander paths traced from rocks in Europe and in North America point to different routes. What assumption makes them agree?

options.label: That the poles never moved at all
That one continent's rocks were mislabelled
That the field was far weaker long ago
That the two continents were once joined

items.explain: The curves could be reconciled if the continents had been in contact up to 200 million years ago, the first clear geophysical evidence for continental drift.

items.prompt: When Wegener proposed in 1915 that continents had drifted apart, why did few people accept it?

options.label: He had no way to explain or trace the motion
He offered no evidence of any kind
Fossils on the coasts did not match
Ships had measured the continents as fixed

items.explain: Despite plenty of circumstantial evidence, no mechanism was known and there was no way to reconstruct the continents' movements.

items.prompt: Tiny magnetic grains drift down through still lake water and settle on the bottom. How can they keep a record of the field?

options.label: They melt and harden again on the lake bed
They line up with the field as they settle
They copy the direction of the water's flow
They turn into new minerals in sunlight

items.explain: Magnetic grains in sediment can align with the field during or soon after deposition, which is called detrital remanent magnetization.

items.prompt: Paleomagnetists also study samples from beyond Earth to learn about ancient fields elsewhere. Which samples?

options.label: Dust collected from comet tails
Light recorded from distant stars
Moon rocks and meteorites
Gas sampled from sunspots

items.explain: The field also measures samples such as Moon rocks and meteorites to investigate the ancient magnetic fields of those bodies.
